### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via AutoEnqueuer (symbol, a top-level class), /api/v1/security/_activation (route, a path literal in declaredWebhookActivationPath), /api/v1/security/_activation/webhook (route, a path literal in reportUnownedRows))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/security/_activation (route, a path literal in declaredWebhookActivationPath))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/security/_activation (route, a path literal in declaredWebhookActivationPath))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via bindDeclaredWebhookNameGuard (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via DeclaredWebhookNameConflictError (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **42** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7e61983e18f9f39dc04ba4255f5a8817af688383` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d761cdad9d2c11ade8e7c68a729fb0733996cb62` — the merge of head `f5a399c56a91d4f003921207f4b9431c6d514aa6` into base `7e61983e18f9f39dc04ba4255f5a8817af688383`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d761cdad9d2c11ade8e7c68a729fb0733996cb62 && git checkout d761cdad9d2c11ade8e7c68a729fb0733996cb62
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7e61983e18f9f39dc04ba4255f5a8817af688383 f5a399c56a91d4f003921207f4b9431c6d514aa6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7e61983e18f9f39dc04ba4255f5a8817af688383 && git merge --no-ff f5a399c56a91d4f003921207f4b9431c6d514aa6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7e61983e18f9f39dc04ba4255f5a8817af688383
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7e61983e18f9f39dc04ba4255f5a8817af688383` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Request: review · area E2 · head f5a399c56a91d4f003921207f4b9431c6d514aa6

## Review — PASS

Head-sha: `f5a399c56a91d4f003921207f4b9431c6d514aa6`
Local-runs: none

**Clause-②: `no` holds (your question).** Every row of the FROM→TO table is a refusal before and a refusal after. 404→409 at the exact and namespace addresses, 404→503 on a failed read, and the name guard, the redelivery veto and the dispatcher warnings changing their text: none of these accepts something that was refused, or refuses something that was accepted. Nothing is dispatched that was not, and nothing written moves. This matches the line drawn on #33491: there a 503 became a determinate *accepting* answer, which is why it was a widening. Here no acceptance moves either way. `patch` on all three packages is right, and `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.

**The change is right.**
- **Remedies name the exact address.** `declaredWebhookActivationPath(name, packageId)` names `?package=PKG`, which switches exactly one holder. That includes two co-owners of one namespace and a package that declares no namespace, where the old namespace address answered 409 or did not exist. The namespace route is not removed, so a scripted call keeps working where it worked.
- **Whole refusal.** `slotsOf` sets `environmentBesidePackage` and `listedTwice` and serves no slot. `listedRefusal(…, whole)` says so instead of "address it by its package". The runtime's `wholeWebhookNameRefusal` runs only once the served slots are none, and reads the plugin's `DeclaredWebhookAmbiguousError` through `packageScopedRefusalOf`'s duck type (`code: RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, `refusal.status: refused`, candidates, message), which that error class satisfies. A miss still answers 404: nothing declares the name, or its only holder is disabled and the bare read returns `null`.
- **Fail-closed.** A failed bare read throws to the door's existing catch and answers 503 with nothing written. In the redelivery guard, a throw from `wholeNameRefusal` propagates, and `assertRedeliverAllowed` turns it into a refusal. "We could not check" never reads as allowed.
- **Guard without `list`.** The name guard with a reader that has no `list` now names each candidate's address instead of a `<namespace>` placeholder.
- Pins: 9 cases cover FROM and TO for every row, and include CONTROLs for two packages listed once each (served, no whole refusal) and for one holder listed twice. With the seven ablations, the coverage is sufficient.

**Notes (non-blocking):**
- N1. Under a whole refusal, a `?package=B` naming a package that does not declare the name at all, and a namespace address whose namespace owns no holder, also answer the 409 naming the holders. Before, both were 404. That is consistent with `not-held-by-qualifier` (also 409 naming the holders) and still a refusal. The changeset's "Same state" row reads as if only the holders' addresses move, so one clause saying "any `?package=` or namespace address" would make it exact.
- N2. The door's whole-refusal pin uses a reader double that throws a duck-typed error. Nothing pins the real `DeclaredWebhookSource` behind the door, so if either side renames `refusal` or `code`, the answer silently drops back to 404. A follow-up pin that wires the real source would close that. It is not needed for this PR.
- N3. `wholeNameRefusal` (plugin) and `wholeWebhookNameRefusal` (runtime) are near twins. The runtime cannot import the plugin, so keeping two is fine.

CI at this head: 40 success, 17 skipped, none failing. The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.

### ⛔ merge queue 构建失败 — 先分诊，再决定要不要重排

队列构建 [43663304554](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/43663304554) 红了。队列跑的是**全量**套件（PR 侧 CI 只跑 affected 子集），
所以失败的测试可能在本 PR 没碰过的包里 —— 那不是重排能修的。每次盲目重排都会让排在后面的所有 PR 重建一轮。

**分类：`failure`** —— 按下面的日志分诊。

**失败的 job（日志抽取，best effort）：**

- **[Test Core (8/8)](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/43663304554/job/132657712273)** — 失败步骤: Run this shard's tests

  ```
  @objectstack/plugin-approvals:test:  FAIL  src/action-page-member.integration.test.ts > [#22578] handleActionPage — the ADR-0043 action page from a Request > GET renders the confirm page for a live to
    ↳ 失败原因: @objectstack/plugin-approvals:test: Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.
  ```

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）

**跨 PR 相同签名（24h，按失败测试文件聚合）：**

- `src/action-page-member.integration.test.ts` — 24h 内已弹出 **8 个 PR**（#33227、#33439、#33444、#33450、#33452、#33463、#33472、#33495），分属 **5 条投机栈** ⇒ **5 次独立命中**。汇总 issue：#33508（已刷新）
- ⚠️ 24h 评论账本**没读完**（超过 5 页仍未读到窗口尽头），所以上面的「不同 PR 数」是**下界**，不是全量。

**历史信号：**
- 本 PR 过去 24h 无队列失败记录（首次）。
- 过去 24h 队列共有 22 个失败构建（不含本次）。

**分诊清单：**
1. 失败测试在本 PR 改动的包里 → 真回归，修 PR。
2. 失败测试与本 PR 无关 → 看上面的「跨 PR 相同签名」；已有汇总 issue ⇒ flaky/环境问题实锤，去那张 issue 上谈，修好前重排只会再烧一轮全队列。
3. 两者都不是 → 可能与同组 PR 语义冲突；等前面的 PR 落地或失败出队后再重排一次即可，不要连续重排。
